review: Reviewed by the mathematician on 23 November 2026 (EV5.1, LP4-11) at 1775302f: the derivation's steps, the reason, the failure example and what an answer does not mean. It found M14 (minor: an empty list means a buffer, since the certified tables cover every non-buffer position), fixed in c152350f. The mathematician's scoped check of 25 November 2026 confirmed the fix on all 35 trees (every non-buffer position has a setup, and no buffer appears) and raised a nit, fixed the same day: at another position the list holds at least one setup. The leaf specifications and test paths are engineering bindings and were not part of the review.

specification.empty_answer: An empty setup list means the named position is a buffer of the orbit's tree: the certified tables cover every oriented non-buffer state of every orbit (solving workflow, section 3.1), so at every other position of the orbit the list is not empty. The empty answer concerns the named position and the table's family only and never says that no solving step exists.

negative_scope.none: the entry answers no yes-or-no question, so it has no negative answer

specification.outside_scope: The certificate covers the shipped tables. A position outside the orbit is refused (`KN2:input.named_object_invalid`); with Jumble on the row refuses (`KN5:input.retained_tool_needs_jumble_off`).

justification.text: The star cycles buffer A to buffer B to the target, so a buffer is never a target of its own tree: the table holds no setup for it. The tables cover every oriented non-buffer state of every orbit, so every other position of the orbit has a setup. The tables are the model's certified execution trees.
